reasoning_summary: Sequential verification of the standard 'g - f lives in G_f' argument. Construction (lines 0006-0013): for each original edge (u,v), h puts (g-f)^+ on the forward residual arc (u,v) and (f-g)^+ on the backward residual arc (v,u), zero elsewhere; well defined since at most one of the two is nonzero per original edge. (i) Capacity (0017-0025): forward, 0 <= g(u,v)-f(u,v) <= c(u,v)-f(u,v) = c_f(u,v) by feasibility of g; backward, 0 <= f(u,v)-g(u,v) <= f(u,v) = c_f(v,u) by g >= 0. Both correct. (ii) Conservation (0026-0113): subtracting conservation of f and g at x gives sum over out-edges of (g-f) = sum over in-edges of (g-f); the per-edge identities g(x,y)-f(x,y) = h(x,y)-h(y,x) (out-edges) and g(y,x)-f(y,x) = h(y,x)-h(x,y) (in-edges) are exactly what the case split gives, and the rearrangement into 'sum of h on arcs leaving x = sum of h on arcs entering x' is algebraically correct, with the residual arcs leaving x being the forward arcs of out-edges plus the backward arcs of in-edges (and dually for entering x). (iii) Value (0114-0158): applying the same per-edge identity at s yields |g|-|f| = sum_y [h(s,y)-h(y,s)], which is the net outflow of h at s, i.e. |h|. Two minor imprecisions do not break the argument: the sentence at 0135-0136 that 'exactly one of h(s,y) or h(y,s) is positive' fails when g(s,y)=f(s,y), but the difference identity still holds with both zero; and the convention at 0116-0125 that s has no inflow only simplifies notation, since with inflow the same per-edge identity gives the general net-outflow formula the proof ends with. Reached the end with no step that fails.
